name: python-dropped-import-still-called-asks
desc: removing `from ulid import ULID` while the new text still calls ULID() is the obs-py-002 pattern → ask. The additive check stays silent here because addInFileDefs folds the OLD on-disk file's import into the known set — proving this ask comes from dropped-import, not the additive check

name: python-dropped-import-removed-and-unused-clean
desc: the import AND every use are gone — a legitimate cleanup, stays silent

name: js-dropped-import-still-used-asks
desc: a removed named JS import still called below → ask
old:
import { fetchUser } from './api';
const u = fetchUser(id);

name: python-dropped-import-relocated-clean
desc: the import line is removed but the SAME name is re-imported on another line in the new text — the refactor-relocation pattern that bench/FINDINGS.md found is the dominant shape among real 'removed import still used' candidates. Every one of those spot-checks (logging, build_report, BASE_RATING) was this, not a bug. If the surviving-import check were dropped, the guard would ask on ordinary import tidying, which is the fastest way to get a default-off check left off

name: python-dropped-import-now-locally-defined-clean
desc: the import is gone and the name is provided by a definition ALREADY in the file — the 'stop depending on the library, implement it here' refactor, seen mid-way through. Pins preBound, the pre-edit binding set, which is computed ONLY for Edit payloads (main.go: `payload.ToolName != "Write"`): a Write replaces the file wholesale, so its bindings all arrive in the new text and there is no prior state to fold. This fixture was first written as a Write and pinned ExtractDefs(newLines) instead — the mutation that killed it removed the whole `bound` lookup, which both folds feed, so the coarser mutation hid the difference. The hunk must contain the USE as well as the import removal: firstUnqualifiedUseLines scans only the added text

name: python-dropped-import-defined-by-the-edit-clean
desc: the import is removed and the SAME edit adds a def of that name — 'replace the dependency with a local implementation', done in one write. Pins the ExtractDefs(newLines) fold, the sibling of preBound: both feed the same `bound` set, so a mutation of `bound` itself would kill either fixture and prove neither. This case existed as a Write, was reshaped into an Edit to pin preBound properly, and that left ExtractDefs unpinned — a gap the mutation sweep caught on its first run. It is a Write on purpose: preBound is not computed for Write payloads, so the suppression here can only be ExtractDefs
